qt: to the Commission Anna Maria Cisint (PfE) Subject:

In the run-up to the local elections in Venezia-Mestre-Marghera, the Democratic Party (PD) has included on its electoral lists candidates from groups with strongly religious overtones. Given these circumstances, incidents have arisen in which electoral support has been garnered by making explicit references to religion, using religious affiliation as a lever to mobilise voters. This raises questions over respect for the principle of the secularism of the state and the principles of pluralism, freedom of choice and non-discrimination of the electorate, which are pillars of the EU democratic order. The case-law of the European Court of Human Rights has made it clear that secularism is a prerequisite for safeguarding democracy. In light also of the recent report by the French intelligence services on the potential for radicalisation among certain groups, there is a need to ensure that the electoral process remains free from all forms of influence. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
Whether it considers these practices to be compatible with the principles of secularism, pluralism and democracy in the European Union?
What steps could it take to help prevent religious pressure or discrimination being exercised on the electorate?
